summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Stonebrook through the Console's trace orchestration, error analysis, and fallback playbooks. Focus on KV cache evictions, prefix caching, tracing correlation ids, VPC integrations, and SLO-driven routing. Customer raised questions about encryption, audit logs, and deterministic replay for audits. Agreed to pilot with a 2-week replay test and run micro-benchmarks on cost/latency tradeoffs.
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-02-28 16:00 PT (61 min)
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lina Park (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Stonebrook - Head of Platform), Ethan Cole (Stonebrook - SRE), Marta Delgado (Stonebrook - Security), Jonas Berg (Stonebrook - ML Eng)
Recording note: Some ASR glitches, speaker turns occasionally misattributed.

[00:00:00] Avery: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick sound check?
[00:00:05] Priya: sounds good, hi all.
[00:00:07] Marco: great, i'll share my screen in a sec, we have about an hour, plan is to walk through tracing -> error analysis -> playbook for fallbacks and then leave time for Q&A.
[00:00:20] Ethan: perfect, we want to focus on how we can reproduce errors deterministically and how rollbacks work, also curious about VPC footprint.
[00:00:30] Avery: nailed it. quick intro on your side priya, what's most important?
[00:00:35] Priya: yeah, we're running a mix: online assistant features backed by a microservice that calls an LLM endpoint via our inference proxy. currently using a managed model endpoint on another provider but investigating Redwood for better cost/perf and private deployment. main constraints: P95 latency under 400ms for short prompts, audit logs for PII compliance, and ability to replay sessions for investigations.
[00:01:00] Jonas: and from ML side we need deterministic request replay with KV cache state control because some failures seem tied to cache behaviour.
[00:01:10] Marco: okay good. i'll start with trace model in the Console — show how we correlate traces across request, cache hits, model variant fallback and logs.

[00:01:25] (screen share: Console trace page)
[00:01:30] Marco: this is a real trace. first bar is request ingestion, then routing, then runtime steps: tokenize -> kv lookup -> kernel dispatch -> response assembly. note the correlation id that follows across services.
[00:01:48] Marta: that correlation id, is that customer-controlled? we need it to map to our internal session ids for audit.
[00:01:55] Marco: yes, you can pass x-correlation-id and we surface it. also we annotate traces with model version, quantization profile, runtime host and GPU id — so you can stitch infra metrics. sometimes ASR labels model name wrong in the transcription but the meta is accurate.
[00:02:15] Ethan: can we log KV cache evictions and the cause? we suspect evictions coincide with higher tail latency.
[00:02:25] Marco: absolutely — eviction events are logged as span events: reason, key prefix, size. you can filter traces by span tag evict=true. we also show a heatmap of prefix hit rates over time.
[00:02:40] Priya: how granular is the request replay? we need to replay with exact KV cache state or force-cold to reproduce.
[00:02:50] Marco: good question. Console supports three replay modes: deterministic (replay with captured KV state), cold (clear cache before replay), and synthetic (inject modified prompts). The deterministic mode stores KV snapshots at chosen checkpoints — note this increases storage footprint but is optional for audit-sensitive flows.
[00:03:10] Jonas: that snapshot retention, is it encrypted at rest and tied to KMS?
[00:03:15] Marco: yes, snapshots are encrypted at-rest with your KMS key when in Private and Dedicated modes; in Hosted we offer tenant keys integrated with managed KMS. we discussed multi-tenant encryption in the doc i think, i'll send the whitepaper.
[00:03:30] Marta: what about access logs for personnel auditing? we need immutable audit trails.
[00:03:35] Lina: the Console has append-only audit logs with RBAC integration to your SSO (SAML/SCIM), and logs can be exported to your SIEM. You can also set retention policies to meet audit requirements.

[00:03:50] (transition to error analysis)
[00:03:55] Marco: next, error analysis. here we correlate application errors, model timeouts, and serving runtime exceptions. see this trace where model fallback happened — we routed to a smaller quantized variant after an OOM.
[00:04:12] Ethan: we saw similar. does fallback affect response semantics? we need deterministic degradation; some fallbacks produce hallucination spikes.
[00:04:22] Marco: correct, fallbacks are model-variant aware. you can configure fallback policies: strict (only compatible variants that guarantee same tokenizer/arch), graceful (allow quantized but with regen fencing), or conservative (no fallback). The Console surfaces expected quality delta and will run lightweight reranks if needed to suppress hallucinations.
[00:04:45] Priya: can we simulate fallback in staging? we want to test user-facing behaviors before enabling in prod.
[00:04:52] Marco: yes, there's a canary rollout tool — you can route X% of traffic to a policy that forces fallback and then compare metrics and captured traces. we also link prompt level evals so you can see quality deltas per prompt group.

[00:05:10] (searching logs)
[00:05:12] Marco: here are request-level logs, the Console binds each request to traces and raw model deltas. note the per-token timing breakdown — tokenization 5ms, KV lookup 12ms, kernel 120ms, network 8ms.
[00:05:28] Jonas: kernel 120ms seems high for our short sequence; is that GPU queuing?
[00:05:33] Marco: likely batching. we have batching telemetry: batch size, wait time, and queuing latency. you can set continuous-batching thresholds and latency SLOs — the platform will trade off batching efficiency for lower tail latency depending on policy.
[00:05:48] Ethan: is there a per-route SLO override? we have some routes that are latency-sensitive and others that can be cheaper.
[00:05:54] Avery: yes, per-route policies exist; you can pin models, set batch caps, and pick routing policies (latency-first vs cost-first).

[00:06:05] (customer reads notes)
[00:06:10] Priya: about private deployment — we will need VPC peering and the control plane to be customer-managed. do you support air-gapped installs for regulated workloads?
[00:06:18] Marco: we support Private with customer control plane, VPC-only traffic, and on-prem packages for air-gapped needs. some kernel-level telemetry requires an agent, but we can run agent in customer env. we'll provide an install checklist.
[00:06:33] Marta: for SOC2, do you provide the standard artifact bundle?
[00:06:36] Avery: yes, SOC2 summary + pen test results available, we'll include them in follow-up. also we have a compliance pack that maps features to controls.

[00:06:45] (deep dive: request-replay demo)
[00:06:48] Marco: demo: pick a trace, choose deterministic replay. starting replay... note the UI shows KV state snapshot restore and then executes request step-by-step.
[00:07:05] Jonas: nice, can we script that? we want to integrate into our CI for regression tests.
[00:07:10] Marco: yes, there's an API — replay endpoints accept trace id, mode, and optional injected prompts. we've seen customers use this in nightly regression to detect quality regressions before rollout.
[00:07:21] Ethan: what about scaling the replay? we need to replay many sessions to reproduce flaky bugs.
[00:07:26] Marco: you can batch replays via the replay API; replay jobs are queued and can run on dedicated compute if you have Redwood Dedicated or Private. for Hosted we limit parallelism but give reasonable throughput.

[00:07:40] Priya: show us a failure hunt example, please.
[00:07:44] Marco: sure. select traces with status error, filter by eviction spans, then correlate with infra metrics — see here CPU spikes on host id 3 and eviction burst right before timeout. clicking into kernel logs we can see a mismatch in tensor shapes triggered by a model variant mismatch — this is often from rolling incomplete model bundles.
[00:08:10] Avery: that's where rollouts tie in — we have canary safety checks that validate signature compatibility. agent note: some ASR popped 'canary safekecks' earlier.
[00:08:18] Marta: who gets access to kernel-level logs? security asks for least privilege.
[00:08:22] Lina: kernel logs are gated by RBAC; you can create roles that only allow metadata and not low-level host debug. We also support time-bound access tokens for ephemeral investigations.

[00:08:35] (discussion: latency/cost tradeoffs)
[00:08:40] Avery: quick example: for a chat route that needs 150ms median, you probably want single-tenant Dedicated with aggressive batching disabled and prefix caching. For newsletter summarization that tolerates 2s, a cheaper quantized model with large batching works.
[00:08:58] Priya: pricing question — do you charge for deterministic trace snapshots?
[00:09:05] Avery: snapshot storage billed separately as retention tier; replay compute billed as replay compute units. Marco will share a sample cost model spreadsheet.

[00:09:18] (objection: vendor lock-in and migration)
[00:09:20] Priya: concern: if we build tooling around Redwood traces and replays, how portable is that?
[00:09:25] Marco: we export traces and snapshots in open JSONL format and provide replay helpers. the vendor-specific parts are in runtime kernels; for portability we provide an export path and migration checklist.

[00:09:40] (Q&A rapid fire)
[00:09:42] Ethan: concurrency limits?
[00:09:44] Marco: Dedicated has configurable concurrency per pool; Hosted has default quotas but you can request increases.
[00:09:49] Marta: retention for audit logs?
[00:09:51] Lina: configurable per-tenant, we do long-term cold storage integration.
[00:09:56] Jonas: can we tag traces with customer tags for cost allocation?
[00:09:58] Marco: yes — metadata tags flow to billing, Console shows per-tag cost breakdown.

[00:10:05] (closing: pilot plan)
[00:10:06] Avery: propose 2-week pilot: we will onboard Stonebrook to a Dedicated pilot slice, run replay regression suite, and test fallback policies. deliverables: benchmark report, tape of traces, and a runbook for incident triage.
[00:10:20] Priya: sounds good. timeline target — start week of 2027-03-07, internal stakeholders: SRE, Security, ML.
[00:10:28] Marta: need to review security pack before kickoff.
[00:10:32] Avery: we'll send SOC2 + KMS notes and schedule a security review with our compliance engineer.
[00:10:38] Priya: one last ask — can we get a short demo recording of the replay flow? for our stakeholders that couldn't join.
[00:10:44] Marco: yes we'll record a trimmed walkthrough and share a link.

[00:10:50] (wrap, final notes)
[00:10:52] Avery: recap: Marco shares replay script and traces, i share security docs and pricing spreadsheet, priya to confirm success criteria. next call: pilot kickoff week of 2027-03-07.
[00:11:02] Priya: thanks all.
[00:11:05] Ethan: thanks.
[00:11:07] Marta: bye.

(remaining ~50 minutes were a hands-on guided session with console, some small silent pauses where customer followed along, plus a 15-min side call between Marco and Jonas to debug a sample trace — covered kernel host mapping and a bug in their tokenization preprocessor; ASR of that side call is lower quality and omitted here.)

End of transcript.
